div.div: One compromised dependency reads every key in localStorage. It cannot read the cookie, because the browser will not hand it over.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 366px; height: 1px; padding-top: 405px; margin-left: 430px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

div.div: CSRF — evil.com posts to your API

div.div: cookie, no SameSite

div.div: withheld

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 350px; height: 1px; padding-top: 515px; margin-left: 432px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-muted);

display: inline-block; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-muted); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The cookie’s own weakness: it is attached automatically, so a forged cross-site request is authenticated too. SameSite is the answer.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 575px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: An HttpOnly cookie trades an attack you cannot fully prevent (XSS reading a token) for one you close with a single attribute (SameSite). That is the whole argument for putting the session in a cookie and the theme in localStorage.
